summary: High Frontier 4 All is Phil Eklund's uncompromisingly realistic space exploration simulation, where players design rockets from real physics-based components and navigate an actual solar-system map using delta-v costs. It's notoriously dense, rewarding careful route planning and technology investment over flashy action.
praised: unmatched scientific authenticity and educational depth
satisfying long-term tech and route planning
modular scenarios scale from beginner to expert
criticised: extremely steep learning curve and rulebook density
iconography and card text are notoriously hard to parse

interaction.kind: shared-map race with claims and tech trading
interaction.detail: Every player's rockets explore and can claim mining or settlement sites on one shared map of the solar system, so a site taken by one player is generally unavailable to another, and patent/technology cards are bid on and traded from a shared market. Despite that shared board and negotiated trades, there is no combat or forced loss of an opponent's pieces in the core game.

scoring.how_you_win: You send rockets to mine, refine, and found colonies across the solar system; the player with the most colonies (plus patents/cash as tiebreakers) when the game ends wins, or in the intro variant, outright first-to-colonize wins immediately.
